papers.title: History of residual stresses during the production phases of AlSi10Mg parts processed by powder bed additive manufacturing technology
papers.abstract: Residual stresses can be detrimental to the proper functioning and the structural integrity of built parts. During the selective laser melting (SLM) process, the scanned layers are subjected to rapid thermal cycles. Steep temperature gradients generate residual stresses. In this paper, the semi-destructive hole-drilling method has been used to measure the residual stresses on AISi10Mg parts fabricated by means of an SLM process. The evolution of the profile of the residual stresses of the samples is illustrated in function of the process phase (as-built, after the thermal treatment, after shot-peening) for samples with and without supports. The outcomes have shown the presence, on the as-built components, of high tensile stresses that the usual post-processing operations are not able to minimise. This paper provides a new knowledge on the history of residual stresses during the production phases of metal parts through powder-bed additive manufacturing technology.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the evolution of residual stresses during different production phases of SLM-processed AlSi10Mg parts.
summary_en.method: Residual stresses were measured using the semi-destructive hole-drilling method on samples with and without supports at various stages: as-built, after heat treatment, and after shot-peening.
summary_en.result: High tensile residual stresses were observed in as-built components, which were not effectively minimized by typical post-processing operations.
summary_en.validation: Experimental residual stress measurements were performed on SLM-fabricated samples to validate the stress profiles.

papers.title: Efficacy of Adjunctive Antibiotic-Loaded Acrylic Bone Cement for Deep Surgical Site Infection Prophylaxis after Primary Cemented Hip and Knee Arthroplasties
papers.abstract: The efficacy of antibiotic-loaded acrylic bone cements (ALBC) for prophylaxis of deep surgical site infections (deep SSIs) after primary cemented joint replacement surgery remains controversial. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the issue, with respect to three types of arthroplasty, namely, total knee arthroplasty (TKA), total hip arthroplasty (THA), and bipolar hip arthroplasty (BHA).
papers.venue: Journal of Orthopedic Surgery and Techniques

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic-loaded bone cement in preventing deep surgical site infections after primary cemented hip and knee arthroplasties.
summary_en.method: A retrospective cohort design comparing infection rates between antibiotic-loaded and plain cement groups across total knee, total hip, and bipolar hip arthroplasties.
summary_en.result: Antibiotic-loaded cement showed potential benefit in reducing infection rates, but the evidence remains controversial.
summary_en.validation: Clinical patient data analysis with statistical comparisons.
